cases.message: the declaration nests too deeply (more than 256 levels): flatten the nesting into separate fields or concepts
cases.note: The parser is recursive descent, and a goroutine stack overflow is a fatal error no recover() sees, so how deep it reads is bounded in every grammar it holds. The remedy is the DECLARATION one: "name its parts as separate statements" is the wrong instruction for a property or a container type. The depth at which an unbounded parse fails is a property of the stack ceiling rather than of the source's size, which is why no byte cap stands in for this.

A concept that does not parse is refused. At boot the concept loader parses each concept on its own and used to drop one that failed with nothing reported, so a node booted without it; it is a skip strict boot refuses now, concept_unparsed (memql#5426). The corpus reads the file with the parser every loader uses, which refuses it here.

A concept whose `{` never closes is refused. The corpus reads the whole file with the parser, which reads the next concept as a field of this one; the concept loader slices each concept on its own, and used to lose this one AND every concept below it without a word, because the unclosed brace left the rest of the file inside it. It refuses this one by name now, concept_unparsed, and builds the note below it (memql#5426).

cases.message: which declares @belongsTo(cluster). A cluster-wide row is inside no account, so a row that follows one has no account to take
cases.note: A @belongsTo via chain is checked where every concept is known, at the engine's load. Each concept here builds on its own; what is refused is the pair. At write time nothing would fail: the row finds no account on its parent, falls through to the call's account and is filed under the wrong one, which is why the tree is refused instead. A parent that declares NOTHING is accepted -- unclassified is not the same statement as cluster-wide (cells/concept/belongsTo holds the single-concept refusals).

cases.message: is not a registered concept. parent= is the canonical id of the concept whose rows the "storeId" field names
cases.note: parent= is the one name in a via declaration nothing else resolves: a via field's @relationship target is resolved, and a missing one refused, by the relationship derivation. The refusal suggests the registered id nearest the one written.

cases.message: the @belongsTo via declarations form a cycle:
cases.note: Each of two concepts following the other says its rows take their account from the other's, so neither is where an account starts, and existing rows could not be assigned parents first. The loop is reported once, walked from the member whose name sorts first. The two relationships are of different types because the relationship derivation refuses, earlier and without a code, two concepts each declaring the same edge type outgoing to the other.
